brief: A system monitor where CPU/memory are organisms — healthy breathes steady, stressed pulses fast

dominant_strengths: Clean dark palette with teal/amber duo creates clear semantic separation between CPU and memory organisms.
Typography hierarchy is confident: bold percentage, quiet uppercase 'USAGE' label, restrained card titles.
Concentric ring motif suggests breathing/pulse metaphor and gives the static frame latent motion potential.
dominant_weaknesses: Static screenshot conveys none of the breathing-vs-pulsing behavior central to the brief — organism metaphor unproven.
Two cards look nearly identical despite 49% vs 68% load; rings should differ in tension, radius, or rhythm.
Tiny status dot in the corner is undercrafted — feels like leftover affordance rather than an intentional vital sign.
fix_priorities: Encode load into ring behavior: amplitude, frequency, jitter — so 68% visibly pulses faster than 49%.
Differentiate the two organism states structurally (ring count, eccentricity) so stress is legible at a glance.
Add a secondary signal layer (waveform, irregular orbit) to deepen the organism metaphor beyond concentric circles.
Refine the corner status dot into a proper heartbeat indicator tied to the same temporal system.
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral surface is competent and behavioral promise is implied, but without visible motion the reflective 'organism' story stays theoretical.
rationale.intent_fit: The frame sets up the metaphor adequately but the still image fails to demonstrate the steady-vs-pulsing distinction the brief requires.
